questions.question: Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation. At the company's annual dinner party, Sonal approached Mukesh, hoping to engage in friendly conversation and mend their strained relationship after a recent disagreement at work. However, Mukesh's responses remained short and dismissive, and he quickly excused himself to join a different group of colleagues. Which of the following best describes Mukesh's behaviour towards Sarah?"
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation.

At the company's annual dinner party, Sonal approached Mukesh, hoping to engage in friendly conversation and mend their strained relationship after a recent disagreement at work. However, Mukesh's responses remained short and dismissive, and he quickly excused himself to join a different group of colleagues. Which of the following best describes Mukesh's behaviour towards Sarah?"
questions.solution:
Sonal approached Mukesh at the dinner party, hoping to mend their strained relationship after a disagreement. However, Mukesh responded with short, dismissive replies and quickly left to join another group of colleagues. This behaviour indicates that Mukesh was intentionally ignoring or being unfriendly towards Sonal, which aligns with the idiom "giving the cold shoulder." It means intentionally ignoring someone or treating them in a cold or unfriendly manner. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Keeping one's chin up: Remaining cheerful or optimistic in difficult situations; staying positive despite challenges.

Hitting the hay: Going to bed or going to sleep; it's an informal idiom for going to sleep.

In the same boat: Sharing a similar situation or circumstance with someone else; facing the same problems or challenges together.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation. Alex diligently completed his homework assignments each night and reviewed his notes regularly. Meanwhile, his classmates often procrastinated, leaving their homework until the last minute and cramming for exams. As the semester progressed, Alex's hard work paid off as he consistently achieved top grades. Which of the following best describes Alex's attitude?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the given situation.

Alex diligently completed his homework assignments each night and reviewed his notes regularly. Meanwhile, his classmates often procrastinated, leaving their homework until the last minute and cramming for exams. As the semester progressed, Alex's hard work paid off as he consistently achieved top grades. Which of the following best describes Alex's attitude?

options.text: A penny saved is a penny earned.
options.html: A penny saved is a penny earned.

options.text: Don't count your chickens before they are hatched.
options.html: Don't count your chickens before they are hatched.

options.text: Bite off more than one can chew.
options.html: Bite off more than one can chew.

options.text: The early bird catches the worm.
options.html: The early bird catches the worm.

questions.solution:
Alex consistently completed his homework and reviewed his notes regularly, showing a proactive and disciplined approach to his studies. He didn't wait until the last minute to do his work, unlike his classmates who procrastinated. As a result, Alex consistently achieved top grades, demonstrating that his early and consistent efforts paid off. This aligns with the idiom "The early bird catches the worm," which means that those who act promptly or start early are more likely to succeed or gain an advantage. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

A penny saved is a penny earned: This means that saving money is just as valuable as earning money, emphasizing the importance of frugality and wise financial management.

Don't count your chickens before they are hatched: Advises against assuming success before it's certain or before all the necessary steps have been taken; warns against premature optimism.

Bite off more than one can chew: Refers to taking on more tasks or responsibilities than one can handle; attempting something that is too difficult or ambitious.

questions.question: Select the appropriate idiom for the given blank. You can argue with him _______, but he won't change his mind.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the appropriate idiom for the given blank.

You can argue with him _______, but he won't change his mind.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'till the cows come home'. The idiom "till the cows come home" means for a very long time or indefinitely. In the given sentence, it describes the persistence of arguing with someone who won't change his mind. Other options do not fit the context of the sentence.

Option (b) is incorrect. "Head and shoulders above" means significantly better or superior.

Option (c) is incorrect. "Standing in good stead" means being in a favourable position or having advantages.

Option (d) is incorrect. "Under the weather" means feeling unwell or sick. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: You can argue with him till the cows come home, but he won't change his mind.

questions.solution:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'under wraps'. The idiom "under wraps" means to keep something secret or confidential. In the given sentence, it describes the government's action of keeping the operation hidden from public knowledge to avoid alerting the suspects. Other options do not fit the context of the sentence.

Option (b) is incorrect. "On the booze" means to be drinking alcohol.

Option (c) is incorrect. "Break bread" means to share a meal.

Option (d) is incorrect. "Rolling in the aisles" means to laugh uncontrollably. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: The government kept the operation under wraps to avoid alerting the suspects.
